# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

## PR Description

Closes #1574
### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite (CI pre-merge scope: `dart test --exclude-tags integration,browser-ext`): **10,547 passed, 10 skipped** (environment-gated live legs), **0 failures**.
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

blocks.text:
# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

- **PR #**: 1585

- **Title**: gh-1574 [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1574` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +390
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:26:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T18:29:44Z

## PR Description

Closes #1574
### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite (CI pre-merge scope: `dart test --exclude-tags integration,browser-ext`): **10,547 passed, 10 skipped** (environment-gated live legs), **0 failures**.
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.
- Release archives are unchanged (`bundle/bin` + `bundle/lib`) — only install destinations moved.

# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). - Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.

Now the key question about the update-path healing claim:

`_binaryUpdate` runs inside the CURRENTLY RUNNING (old) binary's `fa update` command. `_extractAndSwap` calls `copyBundleLibs` — that code is the OLD binary's compiled code. If the old binary is pre-fix, its `copyBundleLibs` copies to `<installDir>/lib` (the wrong location). So a broken install running `fa update` from a pre-fix binary:
1. Swaps in the NEW binary (correct).
2. Copies libs to the OLD wrong location (`<installDir>/lib`).
3. New binary still can't find libs at `<exe_dir>/../lib`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

## PR Description

Closes #1574
### Root Cause

`package:sqlite3` 3.x ships SQLite via Dart **native assets**: an AOT binary built with `dart build cli` resolves its bundled library at `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>`. Every POSIX installer copied the libs beside the binary instead (`<install_dir>/lib`), so for `~/.local/bin/fa` the resolver looked in `~/.local/lib` and found nothing — the first `sqlite3_*` FFI call threw the raw `Couldn't resolve native function … Failed to load dynamic library '~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib'` error. Verified by relocating a real `dart build cli` bundle: `<exe_dir>/../lib` loads, the installer layout fails with exactly the reported error.

### Fix

- `site/install.sh`: copy bundle libs to `$install_dir/../lib` (also the macOS quarantine-xattr pass and the source-build advice lines).
- `install_local.sh`: same — `mkdir -p`/`cp -R` target `$INSTALL_DIR/../lib`.
- `bin/self_manage.dart`: `_copyBundleLibs` → public `copyBundleLibs`, targeting `<installDir>/../lib` (fixes `fa update`; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was already correct since it installs the exe under `<root>\bin\`).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine.dart`: a dart:ffi library-load failure now degrades to a clean `SQLite is unavailable … reinstall or run fa update` note (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` + `sqliteUnavailableMessage` in `sqlite_reader.dart`) instead of the raw resolver dump; database-level errors pass through untouched. A Dart-level system-library fallback is not possible with native-assets bindings (build-time asset mapping, no loader override).
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/sqlite3_engine_stub.dart`: constructor parity for the conditional export.

### Test Coverage

- `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` — new `missing bundled library degrades cleanly (gh-1574)` group: load-failure classification (macOS + Linux error shapes), clean-note mapping through `openReadOnly` and through the `read` tool, non-load errors unclassified.
- `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` — `copyBundleLibs` installs into `<installDir>/../lib` and never `<installDir>/lib`; static layout contract for `install_local.sh`, `site/install.sh`, and `site/install.ps1`.
- Targeted suites: 85 tests passed (`sqlite_engine_test` + `self_manage_test`), all previously failing repro tests now green.
- Full suite (CI pre-merge scope: `dart test --exclude-tags integration,browser-ext`): **10,547 passed, 10 skipped** (environment-gated live legs), **0 failures**.
- `bash scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` (AC1–AC4): unchanged behavior — one pre-existing `contract1b` log-assertion failure reproduces identically on the base commit (environment-specific, not touched by this fix).

### Notes

- Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout). Stale libs at `~/.local/bin/lib` are inert leftovers; nothing reads them.
- Windows `site/install.ps1` needed no change; its layout (`<root>\bin\fa.exe` + `<root>\lib`) already matches the native-assets lookup.

# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

# gh-1574: the binary's native-assets resolver reads <exe_dir>/../lib —

  cp -r "$tmp_extract/bundle/lib/"* "$lib_dir/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# macOS quarantine / signature hardening — runs ONLY after the provenance
# gate above succeeded (SEC-07 #795: no blind quarantine strip). Downloaded
# executables are tagged by Gatekeeper and will be killed on launch unless
# the quarantine attribute is removed. Re-signing ad-hoc makes the binary
# runnable from any directory on Apple Silicon, even without a paid
# Developer ID certificate.
if [ "$os" = "macos" ]; then
  if command -v xattr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$target" 2>/dev/null || true
    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$lib_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  if command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    codesign --force --sign - "$target" 2>/dev/null || true

fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install_local.sh — build the Fa CLI from source and install it locally to ~/.local/bin.
#
# Run from the repo root:
#   sh install_local.sh

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BUNDLE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/fa-local/bundle"
INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"

mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/../lib"

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "→ Building Fa CLI bundle..."
dart pub get >/dev/null 2>&1 || dart pub get
dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local

# gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (the git
# tag is the single source of truth) — stamp the build version from git
# describe: the exact tag when HEAD is tagged, else <tag>-<n>-g<sha>[-dirty].
# A plain `dart run` (no install) shows 0.0.0-dev — acceptable and
# self-explanatory.
VERSION="$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)"
VERSION="${VERSION#v}"
echo "$VERSION" > "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt"
echo "→ Built fa v$VERSION"

echo "→ Installing to $INSTALL_DIR..."
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/bin/fah" "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
chmod +x "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
# macOS ARM kills unsigned native executables; ad-hoc sign so the copied
# binary is allowed to run from ~/.local/bin.
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  codesign -s - -f "$INSTALL_DIR/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt" "$INSTALL_DIR/version.txt"
# gh-1574: the AOT binary's native-assets resolver looks for the bundle
# libs in <exe_dir>/../lib — with the exe at $INSTALL_DIR/fa that is
# $INSTALL_DIR/../lib (e.g. ~/.local/lib for ~/.local/bin/fa), never
# $INSTALL_DIR/lib.
if [ -d "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib" ]; then
  cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/../lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "→ Installed $INSTALL_DIR/fa"

if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "⚠  $INSTALL_DIR is not on your PATH. Add this to your shell rc:"
  echo "   export PATH=\"\$PATH:$INSTALL_DIR\""
else
  INSTALLED_VERSION="$(fa --version)"
  echo "✔  $INSTALLED_VERSION is on PATH"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install_local.sh — build the Fa CLI from source and install it locally to ~/.local/bin.
#
# Run from the repo root:
#   sh install_local.sh

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BUNDLE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/fa-local/bundle"
INSTALL_DIR="${INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"

mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR/../lib"

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "→ Building Fa CLI bundle..."
dart pub get >/dev/null 2>&1 || dart pub get
dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local

# gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (the git
# tag is the single source of truth) — stamp the build version from git
# describe: the exact tag when HEAD is tagged, else <tag>-<n>-g<sha>[-dirty].
# A plain `dart run` (no install) shows 0.0.0-dev — acceptable and
# self-explanatory.
VERSION="$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)"
VERSION="${VERSION#v}"
echo "$VERSION" > "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt"
echo "→ Built fa v$VERSION"

echo "→ Installing to $INSTALL_DIR..."
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/bin/fah" "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
chmod +x "$INSTALL_DIR/fa"
# macOS ARM kills unsigned native executables; ad-hoc sign so the copied
# binary is allowed to run from ~/.local/bin.
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  codesign -s - -f "$INSTALL_DIR/fa" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
cp "$BUNDLE_DIR/version.txt" "$INSTALL_DIR/version.txt"
# gh-1574: the AOT binary's native-assets resolver looks for the bundle
# libs in <exe_dir>/../lib — with the exe at $INSTALL_DIR/fa that is
# $INSTALL_DIR/../lib (e.g. ~/.local/lib for ~/.local/bin/fa), never
# $INSTALL_DIR/lib.
if [ -d "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib" ]; then
  cp -R "$BUNDLE_DIR/lib/"* "$INSTALL_DIR/../lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "→ Installed $INSTALL_DIR/fa"

if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "⚠  $INSTALL_DIR is not on your PATH. Add this to your shell rc:"
  echo "   export PATH=\"\$PATH:$INSTALL_DIR\""
else
  INSTALLED_VERSION="$(fa --version)"
  echo "✔  $INSTALLED_VERSION is on PATH"
fi

Now the key question about the update-path healing claim:

`_binaryUpdate` runs inside the CURRENTLY RUNNING (old) binary's `fa update` command. `_extractAndSwap` calls `copyBundleLibs` — that code is the OLD binary's compiled code. If the old binary is pre-fix, its `copyBundleLibs` copies to `<installDir>/lib` (the wrong location). So a broken install running `fa update` from a pre-fix binary:
1. Swaps in the NEW binary (correct).
2. Copies libs to the OLD wrong location (`<installDir>/lib`).
3. New binary still can't find libs at `<exe_dir>/../lib`.

So the claim "Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update`" is FALSE for `fa update` from a pre-fix binary — it takes TWO updates (the first update installs the new binary; the second update, run by the new binary, copies libs to the right place). The `sqliteUnavailableMessage` even tells users "run `fa update` to repair the layout" — that repair advice fails on exactly the affected population (any install made by the old installers runs the old binary until updated).

Wait — actually, let me double check: which binary runs during `fa update`? `applyUpdate` → `_binaryUpdate` — all in-process of the running binary. Yes, the old binary. The successor is only spawned at the end to resume sessions.

Hmm, but hold on — could the OLD binary even be running with a broken SQLite? Yes — the old binary has the same native-assets binding and crashes on SQLite use with the raw error. The user follows the OLD binary's `fa update`. After the update, the NEW binary is on disk but libs were copied by OLD code to OLD layout. So SQLite remains broken. The user runs `fa update` AGAIN — this time the NEW binary runs, copies libs to `<installDir>/../lib` — now fixed.

So: one `fa update` doesn't heal; two do. IMPORTANT finding (the PR description and the user-facing repair message overstate the healing; the message's `fa update` advice requires the fix to already be in the binary — chicken-and-egg).

Is there any mitigation? `install_local.sh`/`site/install.sh` reinstall works immediately. Also — could the docs/CHANGELOG note this? The PR description says "Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update` (both now write the correct layout)" — this conflates: reinstall writes correct layout (true — new script), but `fa update` from an old binary writes the OLD layout (the old binary's baked-in code). The claim is wrong for pre-fix binaries.

Severity: IMPORTANT. It's not a data-loss/correctness blocker for the fix itself (fresh installs correct), but the user-facing repair guidance is misleading for the exact broken population. Could argue BLOCKING since the ticket's AC says a missing library must produce a clean note — which is satisfied — and the note's advice is wrong. I'll rate IMPORTANT.

Actually wait — one more consideration: is the note shown by the OLD binary or the NEW binary? The clean note is NEW code — only the new binary has it. So a user seeing the clean note IS running a binary that contains the fixed copyBundleLibs. So when the note says "run `fa update`", the RUNNING binary is the new one, whose update path copies to the CORRECT location. 

Wait no! The note only exists in the new binary. But if the user is running the new binary and the libs are missing, that means... how did the new binary get installed with broken layout? Paths:
1. User had old broken install → old binary shows raw error (no clean note). User runs `fa update` (old code) → new binary in place, libs still wrong. User runs fa → new binary → clean note appears → "run `fa update` to repair" → user runs `fa update` (new code) → libs copied to correct location → FIXED. So it works, but takes TWO updates from the broken state, with the first update not healing. The note's advice is actually correct because the note only appears on new binaries!

Hmm, so the note advice is fine. But the PR description claim "Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall or `fa update`" is still wrong: ONE `fa update` from an old binary leaves the layout broken (libs in old place). The heal happens on the second `fa update`. Between the first and second update, the user experiences the bug still (now with a clean note, which then directs them to update AGAIN). So the repair UX is: error → update → error (clean note) → update again → fixed. Confusing but self-converging. And for users who never run update twice, it stays broken.

Is this worth an IMPORTANT? The PR description inaccuracy is minor, but the two-update UX is real. Also, consider: `fa update` from old binary → does the old binary even HAVE `fa update`? Yes, it's an old feature. OK.

Actually, there's one more scenario: fresh installs via the FIXED installers are fine. The broken population is pre-existing installs. The healing path matters for them. I'll flag as IMPORTANT with a suggestion for a better repair (e.g. the note could suggest reinstall, or `fa update` twice / mention that the first update after 1.0.x needs a second one; or have the update flow run copyBundleLibs from the NEW binary — but you can't run the new binary's code from the old process... unless the spawned successor performs a one-time layout repair on boot. That'd be a design change. Alternatively `fa update` could exec the new binary's `fa update --apply-libs`... overkill. Simplest: document the two-update path or have the note suggest reinstall).

Hmm wait, actually there's an even simpler observation: the successor spawn. When the old binary updates and spawns the successor for a live session, the successor is the NEW binary — if the new binary on first boot detected missing libs at `<exe_dir>/../lib` and the old layout exists, it could self-heal by copying `<installDir>/lib/*` → `<installDir>/../lib`. But that's a feature suggestion beyond scope. Keep as suggestion inside the IMPORTANT comment.

For Windows install.ps1: exe at `<installDir>\bin\fa.exe`, so installDir (parent of target) = `<installDir>\bin`, and `installDir.parent` = `<installDir>` → libs → `<installDir>\lib`. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
